1.title: Set Direction & Wrap

2.title: Align Items
2.desc: Set justify-content and align-items to control how items are distributed and aligned

navbar.title: Navigation Bars
navbar.desc: Flexbox is ideal for horizontal navbars — use justify-content: space-between for logo + links

cards.title: Card Grids
cards.desc: Use flex-wrap: wrap with a fixed flex-basis for responsive card grids that wrap on mobile

center.title: Perfect Centering
center.desc: justify-content: center + align-items: center is the easiest way to center anything

form.title: Form Layouts
form.desc: Align form labels and inputs horizontally or vertically with Flexbox for clean, consistent forms

axis.title: ✓ Understand Main Axis vs Cross Axis
axis.desc: justify-content controls the main axis (row direction = horizontal). align-items controls the cross axis. These swap when you use flex-direction: column.

grow.title: ✓ Use flex: 1 for Flexible Items
grow.desc: Adding flex: 1 to a flex child makes it grow to fill available space. Combine with min-width: 0 to prevent overflow in flex children.

gap.title: ✓ Use gap Instead of Margins
gap.desc: The gap property creates consistent space between flex items without adding margins to the outer edges — much cleaner than margin-based spacing.

grid.title: ✓ Use Grid for 2D Layouts
grid.desc: Flexbox controls one axis at a time (row OR column). For true 2D grid layouts where you need control over both rows and columns, use CSS Grid instead.

faq.q1: When should I use Flexbox vs CSS Grid?
faq.a1: Flexbox is best for 1D layouts — distributing items along a single row or column (navbars, button groups, form rows). CSS Grid excels at 2D layouts where you control both rows and columns simultaneously (page layouts, card grids).
faq.a2: By default, flex items are forced onto one line even if they overflow. flex-wrap: wrap allows items to drop to a new line when they would overflow the container — essential for responsive layouts.
faq.q3: What is the difference between align-items and align-content?
faq.a3: align-items aligns flex items within a single row (cross axis alignment). align-content only applies when there are multiple rows (flex-wrap: wrap) and controls how those rows are distributed within the container.
faq.q4: How do I make equal-width columns with Flexbox?
faq.a4: Apply flex: 1 to each flex child. This makes all children grow equally to fill the available space. Use flex: 0 0 33.33% for exactly 3 equal columns regardless of content.
